name: Dorset Community Tree Fund
summary: Grants for community projects that plan, plant and care for trees and hedges in the Dorset Council area, including community orchards, tree nurseries and planting tools. Covers up to 75% of costs for charities and voluntary groups and up to 50% for other organisations.

steps: Application for planning, planting or other eligible work
Road verge planting: get council consent and contact the officer if no plan

eligibility.rule: Community group has a constitution and bank account
Project has some public access or engagement
Planting project uses only plants sourced and grown in the UK
The funded activities do not receive funding elsewhere for the same activity
The funded activities do not fulfil a statutory obligation
A project on private land must have public access
The project is not a commercial project for private financial gain
Has community support and parish or town council support where appropriate

co_finance.applies_to: Charities and voluntary organisations: 25%; all other organisations: 50%

documents: One or two site photos, for planting applications without prior Stage 1
Landowner or statutory permission evidence, where applicable, for direct planting applications
Scale plan of the planting area, for planting projects without prior Stage 1 application
Project budget using the Finance Form or the application’s manual budget table
Evidence of community support, for direct planting applications

status.quote: It will remain open with a rolling application window until all funds are allocated.

applicant_types.quote: The fund is open to organisations in the Dorset Council area, especially parish and town councils, schools, and constituted community groups.

administered_by.quote: The Dorset Community Tree Fund is funded by Dorset Council, co-ordinated by the Dorset National Landscape Team

geography.quote: supports community projects related to planting and caring for trees across the Dorset Council area

access.quote: You can find the guidance notes, application form, finance form and terms & conditions for the fund below.

window.quote: It will remain open with a rolling application window until all funds are allocated.

co_finance_required.quote: The remaining funding must come from match funding, either cash or in-kind or a mixture of the two, but cannot be matched by Exchequer funds

effort.quote: Applications will be assessed within 6 weeks of submission and you will be notified by email.
Is this application for: The planning stage (Stage 1) ☐ The planting stage (Stage 2) ☐ Other

Planting projects on road verges are only likely to be funded in exceptional circumstances and with Dorset Council consent: unless you have already agreed a detailed plan with Dorset Council, you must seek support for planning and design: please contact the Project Officer before preparing your application.

after_award.quote: Before starting your project, you must agree a schedule of interim updates appropriate to your project including any upcoming events, photos of progress or activity and a summary of progress.
Payments will be made following completion of the project and on receipt of a final report and claim form.

documents.quote: attach one or two photographs of the site  evidence of permission from landowner / statutory body if appropriate  extent of public access o details of proposed supplier, species / size selection, and rootstock if planting fruit trees (some trees may be available for free eg from Woodland Trust) o a scale plan of the planting area
Please complete the Project Budget spreadsheet to show a detailed breakdown of costs and funding for your project

Our preferred option is for you to complete the separate Finance Form (an Excel spreadsheet) which will automatically work out figures for you – in which case you can ignore the table below. However, if you would prefer to fill in the form manually then please use the table below.
If you’re ready to go straight for a planting grant we’ll need details including the location and a scale plan of the project, along with evidence of community support and landowner permissions.
